title: Runway impact: headcount scenarios and price/usage sensitivity (Apr 2026)
summary: Scenario matrix that models 3 headcount plans (Aggressive hire, Controlled growth, Freeze + contractors) and 4 pricing/usage sensitivity cases to show impact on monthly burn, ARR, and runway months. Goal: provide exec-level inputs for commit decisions and hiring freezes through FY26.
sheet_rows: HEADER: Scenario, New Hires (FTE), Contractor spend delta, Avg monthly burn ($k), ARR base ($k), ARR change (%), Net monthly cashflow ($k), Runway months (cash at hand = 60,000k)
Conservative price + usage slip, Controlled hires, +18, 120, 5300, 23,100, -3.8, -3,900, 15.4
Price increase + strong usage, Controlled hires, +18, 120, 5400, 25,800, +7.5, -3,600, 16.7
ASSUMPTIONS: Average fully-burdened cost per FTE = $18k/month for eng, $14k/month for non-eng blended; new-hire mix assumed 70% eng, 30% gtm/ops.
ASSUMPTIONS: Contractor spend included when hiring freeze used; contractor rate equivalent to 1.5x FTE pro-rata for short bursts.
ASSUMPTIONS: ARR base shown is current recognized ARR; ARR change derived from price changes and usage growth; elasticity modeled as -0.6 (price) and +0.9 (usage) in sensitivity cases.
COST BREAKDOWN ROWS: Role, Count (new), Monthly FTE cost ($k), Total monthly delta ($k)
Role: Senior SWE, 10, 24.0, 240.0
Role: Mid SWE, 18, 12.5, 225.0
Role: Research/Infra, 4, 20.0, 80.0
Role: Product/Design, 6, 13.5, 81.0
Role: Sales/CS, 8, 11.0, 88.0
Role: Ops/Finance/Legal, 2, 10.0, 20.0
TOTAL new-hire monthly run-rate delta (Aggressive hire) = 734k
TACTICAL LEVERS ROWS: Lever, Impact on monthly burn ($k), Notes
Deferrals (delay new hires by 3 months), -734, one-time, reduces short-term burn but increases hiring pressure later
Partial contractor substitution, +160, raises variable cost but reduces ramp time and hiring commitment
Price increase (+5%), +1500 ARR uplift annualized, modelled as ~125k/month increase in ARR (see elasticity assumptions)
Volume discounts / enterprise deals, -200, negotiated concessions expected to reduce short-term realized ARR vs list, modeled as churn risk in next 6 months
SENSITIVITY GRID ROWS: Axis Price change (%), Usage change (%), Net ARR delta (%), Runway delta (months)
Grid: -5 price, -5 usage, -8.5, -1.2
Grid: 0 price, 0 usage, 0.0, 0.0
Grid: +5 price, +10 usage, +10.7, +1.9
CAPITAL & CASH NOTES: Cash on hand assumed $60M as of 2026-04-01, committed non-payroll runway obligations = $4.2M (Q2 CapEx + support contracts), fundraising buffer target = 6 months of opex.
SENSITIVITY SCENARIO: If monthly burn increases by 20% (unexpected infra spend or pricing pressure), runway falls from 15.8 to ~13.2 months under Controlled growth.
RISK ITEMS: delayed product launches, enterprise contract timing shifts, larger-than-modelled usage spikes by large customers causing burst costs
MODEL LIMITATIONS: does not model monthly billing cadence variability, deferred revenue accounting differences between ARR and cash, nor tax effects on net cashflow
KEY METRICS SNAPSHOT: current MRR = 2,000k, gross margin assumed 68%, net burn pre-scenarios = 3,800k/month, headcount today = 320 FTEs

NEXT STEPS: finance to run sensitivity with alternate elasticity values (-0.4, -0.8), hiring lead times to be validated with Talent and Eng managers, present consolidated slide to execs w/ recommended 90-day hiring pause trigger thresholds
conclusion: Recommendation: move to Controlled growth baseline, implement a 60-90 day targeted hiring hold for non-critical IC roles, allow role-critical hires for infra/ops with strong justification, and surface price tests limited to pilot customers to validate elasticity assumptions before broad rollout.
recommended_actions: Approve Controlled growth scenario as baseline for Q2-Q4 planning
Finance to produce a weekly burn dashboard with top 5 variance drivers (payroll, infra, credits, contractors, enterprise concessions)
Eng/Talent to deliver 90-day hiring spreadsheet by role with earliest start dates and ramp costs
Product/Revenue to run two price experiments: +3% pilot and +7% enterprise packaging test; report impact within 45 days
